goal: Consolidate every owner-facing surfacing spelling of the open-flag predicate onto one composable fragment (openFlagExistsSql) owned by src/lib/moderation/held-draft.ts — the semantic owner of 'is this draft held' — leaving the deliberately-distinct consumers alone with the divergence recorded on the owner module (#725 deliverable, #730 build half).
non_goals: No change to the 8 deliberately-distinct consumers: admin disposition (/api/admin/flagged), admin queue (flagged-service), admin badge (nav-counts-service), health-alert backlog check, offboarding purge-verification + purge-stages + table-disposition, and the producer (response-generation/persist.ts keeps its module-local FLAGGED_RESPONSE_STATUS_OPEN)
No higher-level read helpers — the shape is fragment + retained hasOpenFlag only (#725 §2)
No behavior change anywhere — every rewrite is semantics-preserving
No new CONTEXT.md glossary term — the divergence note lives as a comment block on the owner module (#725 §3)
No shared helper growing a boolean parameter meaning 'actually a different query' (the failure mode this scoping exists to prevent)
No touch to worker/jobs/publisher/held-flag-gate.ts or the other hasOpenFlag call sites — they are already on the owner
user_visible_behavior: None. Held drafts remain projected (SELECTed-not-filtered, D9) on the two draft-status routes and the Reviews list, and remain excluded from dashboard reads, pending counts, and the review timeline — byte-identical result sets
invariants: Invariant #4 as structure: a held draft never surfaces its text or an affordance to the owner — projected sites stay SELECTed-not-filtered (D9); filtered sites keep excluding held rows
hasOpenFlag keeps its exact signature and in-tx post-FOR-UPDATE release-gate contract; none of its call sites move
After migration, the read-side 'open' literal is spelled only inside openFlagExistsSql in held-draft.ts
Tenant scoping of every migrated query is unchanged; ALLOWLIST_BASELINE stays 409 — snippet text regenerates in place, no entry adds or removes
The 8 deliberately-distinct consumers keep their own spellings on purpose
edge_cases: src/lib/agents/read.ts getReviewTimeline: null-filtered anti-join (LEFT JOIN flagged_responses … AND fr.id IS NULL) rewrites to NOT EXISTS via the fragment — must preserve the timeline row set exactly
src/lib/dashboard/pending-count.ts has TWO spellings (per-business count + account-grouped sibling); both migrate

The fragment's correlated ref must compose in three contexts: qualified column refs (resp.id, resp2.id, responses.id) inside LATERAL/correlated subqueries, and hasOpenFlag's ${responseId}::uuid parameter — ref parameter is a Postgres.js fragment, not a string

scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts keys on verbatim SQL source; the SIX entries whose sqlSnippet contains a migrated predicate (past-replies draft-status ~327; load-replies main ~1285; service.ts ~1509 + ~1516; aggregate-service.ts ~1530 + ~1537) regenerate in place in the same PR (the feat-719 gate-block trap, #725 note 1). pending-count has NO entry — its queries are directly scoped; the migration must not add one
The stale D6 comments in draft-status/route.ts and load-replies.ts cite '#680 item' for a consolidation #680 never did — they are rewritten as part of the migration
past-replies/draft-status/route.ts (added by #726, after #725's 6-file table was drawn) carries an inline projected EXISTS — it joins the migration set, making it 7 files / 8 inline spellings

src/lib/moderation/held-draft.ts contract-header comment style — the divergence note extends it
